briefs.subject: Matlock's Fruit Farms
briefs.why: 250 acres, the largest berry farm in the valley, over a million pounds of fruit — and thousands of school-age kids employed over the years, collected by the farm's own fleet of buses. Berries ran to 1987/88, so the youngest former pickers are about fifty and live exactly where we sell.
briefs.textNotes: 🔴 Use the FULL farm name — never the bare word MATLOCK. CBS holds a live trademark and is currently airing a series by that name; a bare MATLOCK shirt risks a marketplace takedown. ⚠️ It is Alderton, not Puyallup — 'Puyallup Valley' is correct, 'Puyallup' alone is wrong. The legal name carries an apostrophe: Matlock's Fruit Farms, Inc.
briefs.designDirection: The buses are the design. Anyone who picked berries in this valley remembers being collected by one. A vintage fruit-crate label shape with a bus in it beats a generic berry badge. Mt Rainier and valley fields belong in the background.

briefs.theStory: Started 1933 on 3 acres on River Road; moved to Alderton in 1945. Three owners across two generations: G. Lee Matlock and his sons David and Ivan. Berries until 1987/88, then tree rootstock; the brothers retired in 1996. In 2015 the 153-acre farm became the largest farmland conservation project in Pierce County history.
